decorates.reason: no decorator/annotation production exists in the pinned grammar. It DOES have the language's annotation mechanism — `modifier_definition` + `modifier_invocation` — and that construct is ADJUDICATED here rather than ignored: applied modifiers are published as `decorators` METADATA on the decorated symbol (SOL-17) and the modifier INVOCATION emits a `calls` edge (calleeKind modifierInvocation), matching the family contract (java's annotations are references+metadata, decorates reserved for runtime callable decorators; C#/F#/Java all treat decorators as metadata on the thing they decorate). renders.reason: no JSX/element-construction production exists in the pinned grammar; Solidity never creates a component-element pair.
renders.vocabularyRuling: extended value (TSX/JSX), NOT APPLICABLE to Solidity.

mixes_in.reason: no mixin/with production exists in the pinned grammar. Solidity's composition construct is inheritance, carried by extends/implements; there is no separate mixin-application production to publish.
mixes_in.vocabularyRuling: extended value (Dart `with`), NOT APPLICABLE to Solidity.

part_of.reason: Solidity's file-inclusion construct is `import_directive`, which IS a module edge published as `imports`; there is no part-file directive that shares one compilation unit's scope without importing (the construct `part_of` exists to distinguish).
part_of.vocabularyRuling: extended value (Dart `part`/`part of`), NOT APPLICABLE to Solidity.

contracts / interfaces / libraries.ruling: each is a published symbol contained by the file-module and (for files at the surface) exported; their ancestors are extends/implements.

inheritance (`is` list).ruling: ONE heritage construct, two readings (SOL-5): non-interface ancestor = extends, in-file interface ancestor = implements. Multiple bases are a list in one specifier, so N bases = N edges.

functions / constructor / receive / fall.ruling: each declared name is read off its leading keyword (SOL-4: constructor/receive/fallback write their literal word), contained by its contract, and is a calls/uses/references scope.

state variables (public getters) / const.ruling: SOL-3: a public state variable is a contained member AND its compiler-synthesised getter is a published member named with its external signature (`bal()`) plus a references edge var -> getter. The getter name cannot collide with a Solidity identifier (no `(` in an identifier).

modifiers (definition + invocation).ruling: a modifier is a contained member; its INVOCATION is a calls edge (SOL-17). Applied modifiers are `decorators` METADATA; there is no `decorates` relationship (see the ruled value).

events / custom errors / emit / revert /.ruling: an event/error is a contained symbol with parameter members; `emit Ev(1)` is a calls edge (calleeKind eventEmission), `revert Err(2)` a calls edge (errorRevert). try/catch clauses are control flow, not relationships (the caught expression's calls/uses are emitted normally).

structs / enums / enum values.ruling: struct/enum are contained symbols with member containment; struct CONSTRUCTION is a calls edge (both spellings, SOL-10), never instantiates.

imports (plain / named / namespace / ali.ruling: the module PATH is imports; an imported BINDING (named or `* as Utils`) is references. Solidity has no export construct, so `import` never pairs with an exports keyword (see the exports ruling).

using-for / using alias.ruling: the using-dependency (library or function list) is a references edge; a call through `using X for T` is a calls edge with calleeKind inFileTypeMember (SOL-15).

object creation (`new`).ruling: `new C()` is instantiates; the type name is read in a type position (references) — instantiates is NOT template/struct construction (SOL-10).

override.ruling: SOL-11 three tiers; the refusals (2+ header bases, no matching declaration) are part of the rule.

Yul / inline assembly.ruling: Yul is a first-class sub-language here: a yul function is a contained member, a yul function call is a calls edge (labels carrying `yul`), a yul identifier / one-segment path read is a uses edge. An EVM BUILTIN is not a user call (SOL-8).

type aliases / user-defined value types.ruling: a type alias / user-defined value type is a contained symbol; type mentions are references (type positions) and a CONVERSION (`uint256(x)`) emits no calls edge — a conversion is not a call (SOL-15).

NatSpec comments / pragma.ruling: RULED: NatSpec documentation attaches to the next declaration as `docstring`/`docTags` METADATA (SOL-16/23) — there is no second symbol to connect an edge to, so no relationship; a pragma is a compilation directive, not a relationship. Both are counted by the D2 census so the ruling is a number, not a silence.

rulings.question: `implements`: is the canonical value applicable to Solidity, given there is no implements clause?
rulings.measured: the pinned grammar has NO implements-clause production (implements_clause / class_interface_clause / super_interfaces all ABSENT — section 2 proves it). It DOES have inheritance_specifier + interface_declaration; the analyzer emits implements from (derived, in-file interface) pairs at :1726 (SOL-5), and fixtures pin the value in both directions (2 positive fixtures, 2 forbid rows).
rulings.verdict: APPLICABLE BY ADAPTED SEMANTICS — an interface ancestor is the contract reading of the one heritage construct. Ruling it non-applicable would contradict the emission and the fixtures.

rulings.question: `exports`: Solidity has no export construct — is the value applicable?
rulings.measured: no export/visibility-keyword production exists for a compilation-unit surface. The analyzer publishes the compilation-unit surface from `source_file` (SOL-12) at :2703; fixtures pin 18 positive export rows in 6 fixtures.
rulings.verdict: APPLICABLE BY ADAPTED SEMANTICS — the value is the compilation-unit surface (contracts/interfaces/libraries/structs/enums/errors; NOT a free function), declared in the rule.

rulings.question: modifiers: is `decorates` applicable (the grammar HAS modifier_definition + modifier_invocation)?
rulings.measured: the value's productions (decorator/annotation/…) are ABSENT; the modifier construct is present. Measured 2026-10-19 in-process: `function f() public onlyOwner {}` emits `calls f -> onlyOwner` with metadata.calleeKind modifierInvocation, and SOL-17 publishes applied modifiers as `decorators` METADATA on the symbol. No fixture expects a decorates row (0 rows across all 31 pairs).
rulings.verdict: NOT APPLICABLE as a relationship — adjudicated: modifiers are METADATA + the modifier-invocation CALLS edge, matching the family contract (java annotations are references+metadata; C#/Java/F# treat decorators as metadata on the decorated thing).

rulings.question: `overrides`: is the override_specifier a real applicable surface, and what does a refused override mean?
rulings.measured: override_specifier is present in the grammar. SOL-11's three tiers are enforced in code (:2528), and the refusals are the rule: a bare `override` with 2+ header bases emits NO edge (the keyword does not say which base declares the member). Measured contract 2026-10-19: `interface I { function f() external; } contract C is I { function f() external override {} }` emits overrides.
rulings.verdict: APPLICABLE — the grammar states the specifier, the language's compiler rejects a wrong `override(X)`, so the edge is the language's invariant; the 2+-base refusal is a declared rule, not an omission.

rulings.question: `uses`: are writes uses, and are parameter reads uses?
rulings.measured: in-process 2026-10-19 on the pinned grammar: `bal = n;` emits uses f -> bal (write) and uses f -> n (parameter read); `return bal;` emits uses f -> bal; `uint256 x; x = n + 1;` emits uses f -> x and uses f -> n. So assignment LHS reads ARE uses (the family write-as-use contract) and parameter reads ARE uses by position — the unresolved mass from parameter reads is the measured binding wall (SOL-FIX §1), not a contract choice.
rulings.verdict: APPLICABLE with the positional-read rule (SOL-2); the parameter-read class is a count, not a silence.

rulings.question: `imports` vs `references`: which construct carries a module dependency?
rulings.measured: `import "./A.sol";` emits imports module -> ./A.sol; `import {B} from "./B.sol"` emits imports for the path AND references for B; `using Lib for uint256` emits references for Lib. The import target is a PATH (measured: the symbol-name guard dropped 357 of 358 imports until the pathTarget opt-out).
rulings.verdict: imports is `import_directive` only (module path); imported bindings and using-dependencies are references.

rulings.question: `instantiates` vs struct construction: is `S({a:1})` an instantiation?
rulings.measured: in-process 2026-10-19: `S memory s = S({a:1});` emits calls f -> S (struct construction, calleeKind external/inFileTypeMember shape) while `new C()` emits instantiates f -> C. SOL-10 states the two struct spellings are both calls.
rulings.verdict: instantiates = `new_expression` only; struct construction is calls (a struct is a value type, not an object with a constructor symbol).

rulings.question: the synthesised getter: is `bal()` a relationship or metadata?
rulings.measured: `contract C { uint256 public bal; }` emits contains C -> bal() and references bal -> bal() — the getter is a PUBLISHED member (SOL-3), not metadata (measured: pool-worker drops symbol metadata at the worker boundary, so metadata would reach nothing).
rulings.verdict: RELATIONSHIP (contains + references), named with the external signature so it cannot collide with an identifier.
